title: Templates and Data Binding
summary: Connect your component's data to what shows on screen.
heading: Templates and Data Binding

blocks.text: Binding is the link between your component class and its template. Data can flow from the class into the view, and events can flow from the view back to the class.

blocks.caption: Class to view with bindings; view to class with events.

blocks.text: Use {{ }} to drop a value from the class straight into the text — just like the template literals from Chapter 6.
Square brackets [ ] set an element's property from a value in your class. Here the button's disabled property follows the isBusy value.
Round brackets ( ) run a method in your class when an event happens, like a click.
A working counter you can edit and run — each click calls a method that updates the value, and the template re-shows it:
Sometimes you want both directions at once — show a value and update it as the user types. The [( )] syntax ("banana in a box") does both.
ngModel comes from FormsModule, so add it to the component's imports.
Here's a working Angular example you can edit and run. The preview uses [value] + (input) — exactly what [(ngModel)] does under the hood — so you can watch the binding update live as you type:
Put #name on an element to grab a reference to it, then use that name elsewhere in the same template.

items: {{ value }} shows a value as text.
[prop]="value" sets a property from the class.
#ref grabs an element to use elsewhere in the template.
